title: Irregular past tense verbs
keyIdea: The past tense tells what already happened. Most verbs add -ed (play, played), but irregular verbs change instead. Many swap one vowel: sit becomes sat, sing becomes sang, get becomes got. Others come in families: bring, brought and think, thought end in -ought; tell, told and sell, sold end in -old; grow, grew and throw, threw end in -ew. A few stay the same (cut, put, hit), and some turn into a new word (go, went). Hided, telled and comed are not words: say hid, told and came.
familyTip: Play 'Yesterday I...' on the walk to school. You say a verb such as sit, tell or bring, and your child finishes 'Yesterday I...' with the past form. If they say 'bringed', say 'brought, like thought' and move on. Keep a list on the fridge grouped by family: -ought, -old, -ew, no change.

visual.caption: Does the verb add -ed, or change? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: sort -ed verbs from changers, swap a vowel tile to make sat and sang, sort past-tense families, fix hided and telled, and finish a diary.

kid: When something has already happened, we use the past tense. Most verbs just add -ed. Today I play. Yesterday I played. But some verbs do not follow that rule. We call them irregular verbs.
Lots of irregular verbs change one vowel. Sit turns into sat. Sing turns into sang. Get turns into got. Dig turns into dug.
Some go in families that sound alike. Bring, think and buy all end in -ought: brought, thought, bought. Tell and sell end in -old: told, sold. Grow and throw end in -ew: grew, threw.
A few stay just the same, like cut, put and hit. And go turns into a whole new word: went. So never write hided or comed. Write hid and came.
adult: Ages 7 to 8. The National Curriculum in England teaches the simple past tense in Year 2 and expects pupils to use it correctly and consistently in Years 2 and 3 (English Appendix 2). The US Common Core standard L.2.1d asks pupils to form and use the past tense of frequently occurring irregular verbs, such as sat, hid and told.

Regular verbs form the past with the -ed suffix. Irregular verbs, often called strong verbs, change in other ways. Many change the vowel (sit, sat; swim, swam; win, won). Some follow a family pattern (-ought, -old, -ew). Some have no change at all (cut, put, hit, let). A few use a different word altogether (go, went; be, was or were). Grouping verbs by pattern makes them easier to learn than one long list.

The most common mistake is over-regularisation: adding -ed to an irregular verb, as in goed, hided, telled or catched. It shows the child knows the rule and is over-using it, so correct it by saying the right form rather than calling it wrong. Be careful with mixed forms such as brang (sing, sang does not carry over to bring) and with using the present by mistake in a recount (yesterday we go).

In the lab your child sorts six verbs into 'add -ed' or 'change', drags a new vowel into sit, sing, get, win, run and dig, sorts eight verbs into four families, taps the wrong verb in four sentences such as 'I hided the key', and finishes a five-line diary about a trip to the beach.

practice.hint: sit is irregular. Change the vowel i to a.
practice.explain: sit changes its vowel for the past: sat. sitted is not a word, and sit is the present.

practice.prompt: A story has {n} past-tense verbs. {k} of them add -ed. The rest are irregular. How many are irregular?
practice.hint: Take the -ed verbs away from all the verbs.
practice.explain: {n} verbs take away {k} -ed verbs leaves {=n-k} irregular verbs.

practice.prompt: Which word is the past of tell?
practice.hint: tell is in the same family as sell, sold.
practice.explain: tell becomes told, just like sell becomes sold. telled is a made-up -ed form.

practice.prompt: Mia fixes {n} verbs that had a wrong -ed, like hided. Each fix takes 1 tick in her book. She ticks {k} so far. How many fixes are left?
practice.hint: Take the fixes she has done away from all the fixes.
practice.explain: {n} fixes take away {k} done leaves {=n-k} to go.

practice.hint: It already happened, and come is irregular.
practice.explain: come changes to came. comed is not a word, and come is the present, which does not fit yesterday.

choices: A verb that does not add -ed for the past
A verb with no past tense
pool.hint: Think of sit and sat: is there an -ed?
pool.explain: Irregular verbs make the past in another way, like sit, sat or go, went, instead of adding -ed.

pool.hint: make is irregular. Say it about last week.
pool.explain: make changes to made. maked adds -ed by mistake, and make is the present.

pool.prompt: Which verb stays the same in the past?
pool.explain: Yesterday I cut the paper: cut does not change. run becomes ran and walk becomes walked.

pool.prompt: Which is the past of think?
pool.hint: think is in the -ought family, like bring and brought.
pool.explain: think becomes thought, like bring, brought and buy, bought.

pool.prompt: A list has {n} irregular verbs. {k} of them are in the -ought family. How many are in other families?
pool.hint: Take the -ought verbs away from the whole list.
pool.explain: {n} verbs take away {k} -ought verbs leaves {=n-k} in other families.

pool.prompt: Which word should replace hided? I ___ the key.
pool.hint: One word, no helper like have.
pool.explain: I hid the key. hidden needs a helper (I have hidden it), and hide is the present.

pool.prompt: Which pair follows the same pattern as sing, sang?
pool.hint: Only one pair is real English.
pool.explain: swim, swam swaps i for a like sing, sang. bring becomes brought, and think becomes thought.

pool.prompt: Which word is the past of grow?
pool.hint: grow is in the -ew family, like throw, threw.
pool.explain: grow becomes grew. growed adds -ed by mistake, and grown needs a helper (it has grown).

pool.prompt: Ben writes a diary with {n} lines. Each line has 2 past-tense verbs. How many past-tense verbs is that?
pool.hint: Two verbs in every line, so double the lines.
pool.explain: {n} lines with 2 verbs each make {=2*n} verbs.

pool.prompt: Which sentence is all in the past tense?
choices: We went out and ate chips.
We went out and eat chips.
We goed out and ate chips.
pool.hint: Check both verbs: go and eat.
pool.explain: went and ate are both past. eat is present, and goed is not a word.
